description:
Found in defk-8qs. All numbers MEASURED UNDER LOAD (two other benchmark agents running, load avg 5-7 on 12 cores; M-series Mac, OTP 29.0.3, 12 schedulers).

Cause (measured): ERTS wakes a sleeping scheduler from wakeup_other_check() (erts/emulator/beam/erl_process.c, OTP-29.0.3, default +sws): at every schedule() on a run queue with waiting processes it adds left_len * (reductions the last process used) + 400 and wakes one scheduler past the +swt limit (medium = 10*CONTEXT_REDS = 40000). A kernel charges 100% of a timeslice (4000 reds) per DEFK_SLICE_US = 250 us via enif_consume_timeslice, i.e. ~14k reds/ms; Elixir doing the same wall time uses ~830k reds/ms (measured: 0.69 ms kernel call = 9.6k reds, 2 context switches; 0.72 ms of Elixir = 597k reds, ~150 context switches). So the wakeup counter of a crowded run queue grows ~50x slower per ms under kernels, and tasks spawned from one process (Task.async_stream refills, or 12 chunks spawned at once) stay on the spawner's scheduler plus 1-3 others.

Dose-response with the slice (48 Task.async_stream tasks x ~0.65 ms, max_concurrency 12, median of 4 rounds x 2 sessions): DEFK_SLICE_US 250: 3 schedulers, 15-18 ms; 100: 7 schedulers, 8.3-8.8 ms; 50: 12 schedulers, 5.8-7.4 ms; Elixir of equal duration: 12 schedulers, 5.3-6.3 ms. +swt very_low (limit 400) with slice 250: 11-12 schedulers, 5.3-6.1 ms; +swt very_high: 2 schedulers, 29-30 ms. +sbwt none/very_long and +sws legacy: no change.

Why not just shorten the slice: one-scheduler cost of yielding vs yield: false (count_primes, median, 3 alternating sessions): slice 250 +3-4% (2M) / +3-5% (0.65 ms call); slice 100 +1-12% / +9-10%; slice 50 +11-12% / +14-18%. Calling :erlang.bump_reductions(4000); :erlang.yield() before the kernel (a simulated yield-on-entry) helped only a little: 15-18 -> 12-13 ms, 3 -> 4 schedulers.

Levers to evaluate (none implemented):
1. A Defk helper for parallel chunks that places tasks with spawn_opt [{:scheduler, n}]: works on OTP 29 (48 tasks: 12 schedulers, 7.2 ms vs 16.5 ms for async_stream) but the option is undocumented in erlang.erl's spawn_opt_option() type, so it may change.
2. Adaptive slice: short slices (e.g. 50 us) only for a call's first ~1 ms, so long calls keep the 250 us cost; short calls would pay the slice-50 cost (~14-18%) above. Needs measuring against bench/yield_cost.exs and bench/tick_gap.exs.
3. Document +swt very_low (elixir --erl "+swt very_low" / vm.args) for apps that fan out short kernel calls: batched_levenshtein 12 chunks 5.1-5.6 -> 2.3-2.5 ms, monte_carlo_rtp 1M 16.7 -> 7.7 ms, cosine_topk 100k 12 chunks 11.7 -> 7.7-9.2 ms; Elixir chunks unchanged within noise.
4. Upstream: ERTS has no NIF API to charge reductions for balancing without exhausting the slice.

Scripts: spread/events/single harnesses described in the defk-8qs comment.

Done when: one lever is chosen (or the guidance in examples/README.md is accepted as the answer), with single-call speed, tick gap and spread measured.

comments.text: Coordinator, 2026-10-11: the documented guidance (Task.async + await_many, bigger chunks, +swt very_low) is the default answer; one lever left to try, as defk-04y (a short slice only when the caller's run queue is crowded). Close this ticket when defk-04y records its decision.

Closed by defk-04y: lever 2 (adaptive slice) chosen and made the default; lever 3 (+swt very_low) stays documented as the stronger VM flag. Decision: ADOPTED as the default (defk-04y). A yielding kernel's function now calls its NIF __defk_native_<name>__ with :erlang.statistics(:total_run_queue_lengths) as an extra last argument; a value > 0 makes the call yield every 50 us (DEFK_SHORT_SLICE_US) for its first 1 ms (DEFK_SHORT_FOR_US), then 250 us as before (defk_slice_init in priv/defk_runtime.h). `use Defk, adaptive_slice: false` opts out. Kernels that never yield are unchanged.

Measured on OTP 29.0.3, 12 schedulers, load average 2.2-2.9 at the start of each block (4-5 during some); treatments interleaved in one VM, medians, two sessions.
(1) Check cost per call (idle / 11 schedulers busy): total_run_queue_lengths 7.8 / 9.3 ns; own queue (run_queue_lengths + nth scheduler_id) 60 / 81 ns; statistics(:run_queue) 43 / 1954 ns; scheduler_id 3 ns. Tiny yielding call count_primes(10): 40-43 -> 49-58 ns (total check), 102-132 ns (own). The NIF API exposes no run-queue length, so the check has to be in Elixir. 9 ns = 0.0014% of a 0.65 ms call.
(2) Lone calls vs 250 us: 0.65 ms -0.6..+0.1% (12 sched), -0.2..-0.1% (1 sched); 2M +0.1..+0.2%: noise. fixed 50 us for the whole call: +8.1% / +7.1% on one scheduler.
(3) Tick gap, one scheduler, 2M count_primes: lone p99 2.25 ms all treatments; with 3 more kernels queued p99 3.2 ms (250 us and adaptive alike; fixed50 2.05). 15 runs of final code: median worst 3.30 ms (250 us) vs 3.34 (adaptive). Slices are never longer than 250 us.
(4) Spread, wall ms / schedulers: 48 x 0.65 ms async_stream 13.6-13.7/3 -> adaptive 5.6-5.7/10-11 (own-queue 5.8-5.9/10, fixed50 5.6-5.7/10-11, +swt very_low 4.4/10-12, Elixir 4.6/11). async+await_many 4.6-5.0/11 -> 4.3-4.5/12. 12 x 0.55 ms 4.2/2 -> 2.1/7 (own 2.4/5, fixed50 2.1/6, swt 1.2-1.3/10-11, Elixir 1.3/11). 48 x 5 ms 35.5-35.7 -> 31.4-31.6 (12 schedulers either way).
(5) Examples (Task.async_stream chunks): batched_levenshtein 12 chunks 3.8-3.9/2 -> 1.9/5-6 (swt 1.0-1.1/9-10); monte_carlo_rtp 1M 48 chunks 12.7/3 -> 5.5/10 (swt 4.6/8-9); cosine_topk 100k 12 chunks 7.7-7.8/5 -> 3.9-4.1/9-10 (swt 3.7/8-9). Recovers 70-93% of what +swt very_low gains; +swt very_low is still 1.1-1.8x better, and bigger chunks / Task.async+await_many stay the first advice.
Didn't help: switching to 50 us inside the kernel after a resume that waited > 20 us (no Elixir check): 12.7/3 vs 13.6/3.

Adoption rule met: the check costs ~0.0014% of a 0.65 ms call, and most of the spread is recovered. Recorded in docs/performance.md 4.9 (4.1/4.3 point to it), docs/guides/runtime-contract.md section 1, examples/README.md rule 7. Benches: bench/run_queue_check_cost.exs, bench/adaptive_slice.exs (single / tick / spread), bench/adaptive_slice_examples.exs; fixed50 and gap columns used the experimental API of commit be24cd7. Tests: test/adaptive_slice_test.exs.

title: Runtime: short parallel kernel calls do not wake idle schedulers (wakeup-other sees 4000 reds per 250 us)
